issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the problem specification, the example usage in Main, nor the solution. The problem UML and the solution define Meal(String, String[]) (name first, ingredients second), and Main instantiates Meal with the name first. However, the template's Meal constructor signature is Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This will confuse students and lead to compilation/errors when following the provided examples and the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust the constructor body accordingly so it matches the UML in the problem statement, the example usage in Main, and the solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution define the Meal constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal class declares the constructor with the parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This mismatch between the documented/expected constructor signature and the template implementation (and the fact that Main in the template instantiates Meal using the name-first order) creates a mapping confusion for students: they may follow the problem description or the Main usage and find the template's constructor signature inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Meal constructor to match the problem statement and solution: change the signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Update any template code that relied on the reversed parameter order if necessary (the commented Main already uses name-first and will then be consistent).
